rationale: The proposed topology improves the binding constraints—primarily NF and S21—by introducing a source-degenerated common-source stage with an inductor-loaded resonant network, which enhances gain and noise performance while maintaining input match. The addition of an inductor in the drain path of M1 forms a resonant tank at 5.8 GHz, boosting S21 and reducing NF by increasing the effective transconductance gain while preserving input impedance. The degeneration resistor (modeled as a small R) is omitted to avoid noise penalty, and the topology remains fully passive in the signal path, ensuring low power and high stability. This design leverages the 45nm process’s low parasitics to achieve narrowband resonance without excessive inductor count, satisfying the tight NF and gain requirements.
